title: Adjective and preposition patterns
titleVi: Tính từ và giới từ đi kèm
summary: Cặp tính từ + giới từ cố định, khung It is ... to ..., và sự khác biệt afraid to do / afraid of doing.
whyItMatters: Giới từ không theo quy luật nào — nó thuộc về từng tính từ, nên giám khảo coi đây là thước đo chính xác từ vựng. *Interested on*, *good in*, *married with* là những lỗi nhỏ nhưng xuất hiện dày đặc, và mỗi lỗi đều làm giảm điểm Lexical Resource vì người đọc thấy bạn chưa kiểm soát được cụm từ.

sections.heading: Adjective + to-infinitive: two frames
body: The impersonal frame **It is + adjective + to do** lets you comment on a whole action: *It is difficult to measure happiness*, *It would be unwise to ignore these figures.* This is one of the most useful evaluation structures in Task 2.

The same meaning can be personal: **subject + be + adjective + to do**. *It is hard to understand him* becomes *He is hard to understand* — and note that the pronoun **disappears**. *He is hard to understand it* is wrong.

The pattern also works with a noun in the middle: *a difficult question to answer*, *an easy mistake to make*, *a good place to start*. This compresses a relative clause and sounds noticeably more advanced.

rows: It is + adj + to do
It is unrealistic to expect immediate results.
Subject + be + adj + to do
The data is hard to interpret.
adj + noun + to do
This is a difficult trend to reverse.
the first/last/only + to do
She was the first to question the figures.
sure/likely/bound + to do
Prices are likely to rise again.

sections.heading: of somebody or for somebody?
body: Use **of** when the adjective describes the person's character: *It was kind of you to help*, *It was careless of me to forget*, *silly, stupid, generous, thoughtful, rude, polite* all take *of*.

Use **for** when the adjective describes the situation rather than the person: *It is important for students to read widely*, *It was difficult for her to concentrate*, *necessary, essential, possible, unusual, normal* take *for*.
The test is simple: if you can say "that was a kind/careless act", use **of**. If the adjective would describe a situation, use **for**.

examples.right: It was generous of them to fund the whole project.
examples.wrong: It was generous for them to fund the whole project.

examples.right: It is essential for governments to act before 2030.
examples.wrong: It is essential of governments to act before 2030.

examples.right: It was stupid of me to leave the passport at home.
examples.note: Self-criticism with **of** is the natural idiom.

sections.heading: Adjective + preposition: learn them as pairs
body: Many adjectives are locked to one preposition, and the choice is arbitrary: **interested in, good at, afraid of, capable of, responsible for, aware of, dependent on, familiar with, keen on, opposed to, committed to, similar to, different from, married to**.

After a preposition, a verb must be in the **-ing** form: *interested in learning*, *capable of managing*, *responsible for collecting*, *committed to reducing*. This is why *look forward to see* is wrong — *to* here is a preposition, not part of an infinitive.

Some adjectives take both a preposition and a to-infinitive with a change of meaning: *sorry for doing* (apologising) against *sorry to hear* (reacting to news); *interested in doing* against *interested to hear/see/know* (curiosity about a fact).

rows: interested in + -ing
She is interested in studying abroad.
good / bad at + -ing
He is good at explaining complex ideas.
afraid of + -ing
Many people are afraid of flying.
capable of + -ing
The system is capable of processing thousands of forms.
responsible for + -ing
The ministry is responsible for enforcing the rules.
aware of / opposed to
Voters are aware of the costs and opposed to the tax.
dependent on / familiar with
The region is dependent on tourism.
committed to + -ing
The company is committed to cutting waste.
married to / similar to / different from
Her approach is similar to mine.

sections.heading: afraid to do and afraid of doing
body: **afraid to do** means you avoid the action because it feels dangerous: *She was afraid to swim in the river.* **afraid of doing** means you fear the consequence: *She was afraid of falling.* In practice *afraid of -ing* is far more common, and it is the safe default.

The same logic separates **sorry to do** (regret about news you are giving) from **sorry for doing** (apology for your own action): *I'm sorry to tell you that the grant was refused* versus *I'm sorry for missing the meeting.*

**interested to hear/see/know** reports a reaction to information: *I was interested to learn that the scheme had failed.* **interested in -ing** reports a lasting interest: *I'm interested in learning Portuguese.*

examples.right: I'm sorry to hear about your father.
He was afraid of being rejected, so he never applied.
examples.wrong: He was afraid to being rejected, so he never applied.

sections.heading: Verb + preposition + -ing: the same machinery
body: Verbs behave identically. Two lists cover most of what you need. Without an object: **approve of, decide against, dream of, feel like, insist on, look forward to, succeed in, think of/about, end up**. *They succeeded in cutting costs by 12%.*

With an object: **accuse somebody of, congratulate somebody on, prevent somebody from, stop somebody from, suspect somebody of, thank somebody for, blame somebody for**. *The weather prevented us from finishing the survey.*

One verb deserves special attention: **apologise to somebody for something**. It needs both prepositions, in that order — *She apologised to the class for the delay.* Learners frequently drop the first one.

examples.right: I look forward to hearing from you.
examples.wrong: I look forward to hear from you.

examples.right: They accused the firm of misleading customers.
She apologised to the committee for submitting the report late.
examples.wrong: She apologised the committee for submitting the report late.

commonMistakes.wrong: He is very good in mathematics.
commonMistakes.right: He is very good at mathematics.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *giỏi về* dẫn tới *good in/about*. Cụm cố định là **good at** (và **bad at**), không có ngoại lệ.

commonMistakes.wrong: I am interested on studying abroad.
commonMistakes.right: I am interested in studying abroad.
commonMistakes.why: *Quan tâm đến* khiến người học chọn *on* hoặc *about*. Cụm đúng là **interested in + -ing**.

commonMistakes.wrong: It was very kind for you to help me.
commonMistakes.right: It was very kind of you to help me.
commonMistakes.why: **kind** mô tả phẩm chất con người nên dùng **of you**, không dùng *for*. *For* chỉ dùng với tính từ mô tả tình huống (*important, necessary, difficult*).

commonMistakes.wrong: This question is difficult to answer it.
commonMistakes.right: This question is difficult to answer.
commonMistakes.why: Trong cấu trúc **adj + to V**, tân ngữ đã là chủ ngữ của câu nên không lặp lại đại từ. Tiếng Việt *khó trả lời nó* khiến người học thêm *it*.

commonMistakes.wrong: I look forward to see you next week.
commonMistakes.right: I look forward to seeing you next week.
commonMistakes.why: Trong **look forward to**, *to* là giới từ chứ không phải dấu hiệu nguyên mẫu, nên phía sau phải là **-ing**. Đây là lỗi rất phổ biến trong email và thư.

ieltsTips: Dùng khung `It is + adj + to do` để đánh giá trong Task 2: `It is unrealistic to expect all students to attend university.`
Học tính từ theo cụm hoàn chỉnh trong sổ tay: `capable of -ing`, `committed to -ing`, `responsible for -ing` — đừng học từ đơn.
`be likely to`, `be bound to`, `be the first to` là ba cấu trúc Band 7.5+ giúp câu dự đoán và xếp hạng nghe tự nhiên.
Trong thư học thuật, `I look forward to hearing from you` là câu kết chuẩn — nhớ **-ing**.

exercises.question: The region is heavily dependent ___ tourism.
It was careless ___ me to leave the document unsigned.
exercises.explanation: **careless** mô tả phẩm chất người → **of me**.

exercises.question: The company is committed ___ its carbon emissions by 40%.
Many graduates are afraid ___ their first interview.
exercises.explanation: Sợ hậu quả → **afraid of + -ing**; *afraid to fail* cũng tồn tại nhưng ít tự nhiên ở đây.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: It is important of us to act now.
It is important for us to act now.
It is important to us acting now.
It is important that us to act now.
exercises.explanation: Tính từ mô tả tình huống dùng **for + tân ngữ + to V**.

exercises.question: She is very good ___ (prep) managing large teams.
I am looking forward to ___ (hear) from you.
The storm prevented the team from ___ (complete) the survey.
This is a difficult problem ___ (solve) without more data.
exercises.explanation: **adj + noun + to-infinitive**: *a difficult problem to solve*.

exercises.question: He apologised ___ (prep) the class for arriving late.
